auditor: independent AI auditor (did not write the paper); a fresh one for every round

audits.summary: Runs are real and bit-reproducible, the code matches the paper, baselines are fair, citations are verified, and every stated number matches the tables; the negative result is framed honestly. One fixable major issue: two extra main-cell seeds (5, 6) were run and plotted but their outcomes, which go against the headline direction (uniform 0/2, curriculum 1/2; pooled 3/7 vs 2/7, p about 0.22), are not reported, and some wording presumes a curriculum 'loss' the data do not establish.

findings.issue: The 'curves' group ran seeds 5 and 6 with the identical main-cell configuration; outcomes (uniform 0/2 reached, curriculum 1/2 at 2750 steps, anti-curriculum 1/2) are not reported although the runs are used for Fig. 2. Pooled over 7 seeds: uniform 3246 (3/7), curriculum 3789 (2/7), anti 3993 (2/7), Welch p=0.22, paired p=0.27. The omitted runs halve the headline gap and undercut 'so the loss is not specific to operand size' and 'growing a pool slowly is costly regardless of the order', which presume a loss versus uniform that is not significant.
findings.fix: Report the seed 5/6 outcomes and the pooled 7-seed numbers as a post-hoc check next to the registered 5-seed test; reword the abstract and ablation sentences to say that no ordering showed a benefit and that the supported pacing effect is within the curriculum family (T_c=250 vs 1000).

findings.issue: The T_c=2000 and T_c=4000 rows are confounded with the fixed 4000-step budget (pool not full until late; train95 at about 1875 and 3700), so 0/5 and 1/5 reached there is partly by construction, yet they are presented as part of a monotone degradation.
findings.fix: State the budget confound explicitly, or report steps after full exposure, or run those rows with a longer budget.

findings.issue: 72 grid rows were relabelled after the fact (group grid to main, kind ablation to method/baseline); metrics and provenance are unchanged, but the registry now disagrees with experiments/run_all.sh, PROTOCOL.md, log filenames, results/tables/grid.md and the paper's description of a separate grid group.
findings.fix: Revert the relabel and have analysis/make_tables.py read group grid, or document the relabel in PROTOCOL.md and RESULTS.md and regenerate grid.md.

findings.issue: The roughly ten pilot runs (seed 100), including the claim that lr 1e-3 did not generalise within 6000 steps, have no registry rows or logs, so the claim is unverifiable.
findings.fix: Re-run the pilot runs through rh run and register them, or remove the specific 6000-step claim.

findings.where: paper/sections/results.tex ('Where grokking is and is not seen')
findings.issue: 'waits about 2820 steps (grok_gap)' is a censored mean that includes two uniform seeds that never generalised (one with final train accuracy 0.795); among the three that reached 95% the gap is 2133.
findings.fix: Say the grok_gap means are censored lower bounds and give the gap for runs that reached 95%.

findings.issue: 'All of these vary weight decay or data size under random mini-batches' and 'the standard recipe in grokking studies [1],[2]' are inaccurate: Gromov's abstract describes vanilla (full-batch) gradient descent, Nanda et al. also train full-batch (from memory, not re-fetched), and Mohamadi et al. is theory.
findings.fix: Reword to 'none of these manipulates the order of training examples' and cite only Power et al. for the mini-batch recipe.

findings.issue: RESULTS.md says 'so the ordering by operand size is not what helps or hurts', which is stronger than 0/5 vs 1/5 supports; the VERDICT.md ablation table shows 'missing' for every row; Fig. 2's y-axis is labelled 'value'.
findings.fix: Soften the RESULTS.md sentence, fill or remove the ablation table, and label the axis 'held-out accuracy'.

findings.issue: Running the mandated 'rh lit verify' rewrote the checked_at timestamp, leaving the file modified in git (audit side effect, not an author error).
findings.fix: Run 'git checkout paper/citations.json' or commit the refreshed timestamp.

audits.summary: The paper honestly reports a negative result: every number in the prose and tables was recomputed from results/runs.jsonl and matches, all 119 runs have commands and logs whose metrics equal the registry, and two re-executed main-cell runs reproduced the registry values exactly. Code matches the described method, baselines share data and budget, citations are used in context, and the 6-page PDF renders cleanly. Only minor issues remain: an untested post-hoc pacing contrast, one ambiguous sentence in the conclusion, a disclosed hand relabel of registry rows, and housekeeping.

findings.issue: The claim that the pacing sweep 'does support' an effect within the curriculum family (T_c=250 vs 1000) and the sentence 'Shorter curricula are better' are given without any reported test; it is one post-hoc contrast chosen from five pacing levels with 5 seeds (auditor computed Welch p=0.031, paired p=0.029, Fisher p=0.048, uncorrected).
findings.fix: Report the test for T_c=250 vs 1000, label it post hoc and uncorrected, and soften 'Shorter curricula are better' to a descriptive statement.

findings.issue: 'two further seeds run afterwards reversed its direction' can be read as the pooled effect reversing; the pooled 7-seed means still have the curriculum slower (3789 vs 3246), only seeds 5-6 on their own went the other way.
findings.fix: Reword as in the abstract: the two extra seeds went the other way and the pooled gap shrinks from 1010 to 543 steps, not significant.

findings.issue: 72 grid rows in the 'append-only' registry were hand-relabelled from group grid/kind ablation to group main/kind method or baseline (metrics and provenance verified unchanged, and disclosed); rh status now shows main as 9 tasks, and stale or meaningless harness tables remain (grid.md, grid.tex, sweep_warm pooled over all T_c with n=20).
findings.fix: Revert the relabel and have analysis/make_tables.py read group grid, or delete the stale tables and drop 'append-only' from the README.

findings.issue: results/raw is git-ignored, so the curve CSVs behind Fig. 2 and the raw metric JSONs are not in the repository; analysis/pooled.py cannot regenerate Fig. 2 from a fresh clone.
findings.fix: Commit the six curve CSVs or state that Fig. 2 requires re-running the six deterministic curves commands.

findings.issue: Limitations do not explicitly say the task is a synthetic algorithmic toy whose conclusions may not transfer to natural data.
findings.fix: Add one sentence on the synthetic-task scope.

findings.issue: PROTOCOL says '<=25 s/run' but the longest run took 32.7 s (the paper says about 30 s); state.json says the paper is 5 pages but the PDF has 6.
